raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The figure is a grouped bar chart illustrating the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two distinct configurations: “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer,” as indicated in the legend. The horizontal axis, labeled “Sparsity Rate,” displays categorical values ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is logarithmically scaled and spans from 10¹ to 10³, with major gridlines at powers of ten. For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars are shown: a blue bar representing “Per-Output” and an orange bar representing “Per-Layer.” At lower sparsity rates (10%–50%), both bars remain relatively low and close in height, with perplexity values near or slightly above 10¹. As sparsity increases to 60%, both bars rise slightly, with the orange “Per-Layer” bar becoming marginally taller. At 70% sparsity, both bars increase further, with the orange bar again slightly exceeding the blue. At 80% sparsity, both bars reach their maximum heights, with the orange bar visibly taller than the blue, both exceeding 10² and approaching 10³. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, outlines, or annotations beyond their color coding and positioning.

raw_responses.Chinese:
This bar chart displays the relationship between Sparsity Rate and Perplexity for two distinct computational methods, labeled "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," with the vertical axis representing Perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3 and the horizontal axis showing Sparsity Rate as categorical percentages from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. The chart features grouped bars for each Sparsity Rate category, where the blue bar corresponds to the "Per-Output" method and the orange bar to the "Per-Layer" method, as indicated by the legend in the upper left. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 50%), both methods exhibit low and nearly identical perplexity values, approximately 5. As the sparsity rate increases to 60%, 70%, and 80%, both methods show a marked increase in perplexity, with the "Per-Layer" method consistently yielding higher perplexity than "Per-Output" at each sparsity level; for instance, at 80% sparsity, the "Per-Output" perplexity is approximately 500 while the "Per-Layer" perplexity exceeds 1000. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate along the horizontal axis, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines is applied to any specific bar or group.

raw_responses.English:
This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different methods: “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend, which assigns blue bars to “Per-Output” and orange bars to “Per-Layer.” The horizontal axis, labeled “Sparsity Rate,” displays eight discrete categories ordered from left to right as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is logarithmically scaled and spans from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), with major gridlines and tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. For each sparsity rate, two adjacent vertical bars are plotted: the left bar represents “Per-Output” and the right bar represents “Per-Layer.” At 10% sparsity, both bars are approximately at a perplexity of 5. At 20% and 30%, both bars remain near 5. At 40% and 50%, both bars are slightly above 5. At 60%, the “Per-Output” bar reaches approximately 8 and the “Per-Layer” bar reaches approximately 10. At 70%, the “Per-Output” bar rises to approximately 15 and the “Per-Layer” bar to approximately 30. At 80%, the “Per-Output” bar reaches approximately 400 and the “Per-Layer” bar reaches approximately 800. All bars increase in height as sparsity rate increases, with the “Per-Layer” bars consistently taller than the “Per-Output” bars at each sparsity level, and both sets of bars show a steepening increase in height beyond 60% sparsity. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, outlines, or annotations beyond their color coding and position.

raw_responses.German:
Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Perplexity-Werte zweier Methoden — „Per-Output“ und „Per-Layer“ — über verschiedene Sparsitätsraten von 10 % bis 80 %. Die horizontale Achse stellt die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent dar, mit gleichmäßig verteilten Kategorien von 10 % bis 80 % in 10 %-Schritten. Die vertikale Achse zeigt die Perplexity auf einer logarithmischen Skala, die von 10¹ bis 10³ reicht, mit horizontalen gestrichelten Linien bei 10¹, 10² und 10³ als Referenz. Jede Sparsitätsrate hat zwei nebeneinander angeordnete Balken: der linke, blau gefärbte Balken repräsentiert „Per-Output“, der rechte, orange gefärbte Balken „Per-Layer“. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern folgen der Reihenfolge der Sparsitätsraten von links nach rechts. Bei niedrigen Sparsitätsraten (10 %–50 %) sind beide Balken sehr kurz und liegen nahe bei 10¹; ab 60 % steigen die Werte an, wobei der „Per-Layer“-Balken stets höher ist als der „Per-Output“-Balken. Bei 80 % Sparsitätsrate erreicht der „Per-Output“-Balken etwa 500 (zwischen 10² und 10³), während der „Per-Layer“-Balken knapp über 1000 liegt. Die Legende oben links identifiziert die Farben und Bezeichnungen der beiden Datenreihen.
